sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美美元金融中枢、私人利益基金会（PIF）与运河船舶登记

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Offshore Trade Intermediary and Commercial Re-Invoicing Operations

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 23 de 27 de abril de 2010 (Ley 23 de 2010) and implementing regulations, notably Executive Decree No. 209 of 4 February 2020 creating the Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF); additionally, Resolución No. 201-2020 of the Registro Público de Panamá and the Unidad de Análisis Financiero (UAF) AML/CFT regulations including risk-based approach rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (POA) empowering the Panamanian registered agent to incorporate the Private Interest Foundation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or competent authority in the founder's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of valid passport of each founder, council member, protector and initial beneficiary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary or embassy/consulate in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing or equivalent legal-entity evidence for any corporate founder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registrar of the founder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and source-of-funds statement
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization if originating from a non-Hague Convention state

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all applicants, founders, UBOs and protectors against the OFAC SDN list, UN Consolidated Sanctions List, EU Consolidated Sanctions List, HM Treasury Sanctions List, and Panama's List of Terrorists and Terrorist Organizations maintained by the UAF; mandatory Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) identification and enhanced due diligence under Law 23 of 2010 (as amended) and UAF regulatory guidelines; continuous source-of-funds verification and transaction monitoring are required for all PIF incorporations in the medium-risk re-invoicing category.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – Online Name Reservation Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The foundation name must be submitted in Spanish, or in Latin-script characters with transliteration into Spanish phonetics if derived from a non-Latin script. The name must include the suffix 'Fundación', 'Fundación de Interés Privado' or 'Fundación Privada' to identify the legal form; it must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing registered name and must comply with the Registry's guidelines on corporate nomenclature.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a reconsideration request (recurso de reconsideración) with the Registro Público within five business days; if rejected, an appeal (recurso de apelación) may be filed with the Director General of the Registro Público within the next five business days. A formal judicial challenge (demanda contencioso-administrativa) may be brought before the Sala Tercera of the Supreme Court within two months. Name reservations may be extended once for an additional thirty days upon payment of the applicable renewal fee.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office arrangements are acceptable only when provided by a licensed Panamanian resident agent that maintains a physical street address, staff, and records within Panama. A pure mail-forwarding or email-only address fails substance requirements. For ISIC 4690 re-invoicing operations, the tax authority and banking counterparties will require demonstrable commercial substance including employment of qualified personnel, contractual management, invoicing systems, and bank management in Panama.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate-low: approximately 15% within the first three years of operation, rising to 25% or higher upon detection of risk indicators such as inconsistent re-invoicing margins, complex cross-border fund routing, or UBOs from high-risk jurisdictions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff for name reservation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation and notarization of the foundation charter and deed of incorporation by a Panamanian attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Notary of the First Circuit (Panama City) and authorized attorney
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for PIF incorporation documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Filing and inscription fees for the foundation deed and subsequent registry filings
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official registry tariff calculated on the stated foundation patrimony

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered agent and resident agent service fee for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for licensed registered-agency services

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization of foreign UBO documentation
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Original-country apostille authority or local consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Standard per-document apostille or legalization fee

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: AML/CFT PEP and sanctions screening compliance package for founders and UBOs
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: AML compliance consultant or licensed compliance service provider
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market-based professional fee or per-screen data provider tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO declaration initial filing fee with the Beneficial Owner Registry (RBF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Registro de Beneficiarios Finales (RBF)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory administrative fee per initial declaration

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Taxpayer registration (RUC) and public invoice authorization for commercial re-invoicing
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) del Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registration and taxpayer-ID issuance tariff

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Private Interest Foundations Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995, as amended by Law No. 31 of 2011, and Executive Decree regulating the Public Registry, together with the complementary provisions of the Civil Code and the Code of Commerce applicable to foundations; Articles 1, 6, 12, and 18-25 of Law No. 25 of 1995.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá), Mercantile Section, Private Interest Foundations Docket.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta de Constitución / Escritura Pública de Fundación de Interés Privado), executed as a notarized private instrument or public deed and submitted for inscription in the Foundations Volume.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Law No. 25 of 1995 prescribes no minimum statutory paid-up capital; the Foundation Charter must declare a real and quantified initial patrimony, commonly between USD 10.00 and USD 10,000.00. No mandatory escrow is imposed by statute, but incorporating counsel customarily holds the initial patrimony in a segregated trust/escrow account of the Foundation Council and delivers a written discharge receipt as registration evidence.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, at the first session of the Foundation Council of [Foundation Name], Foundation No. [___], that the Council accepts the Founder's endowment of [USD ___], acknowledged as the initial patrimony of the Foundation. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the statutory seat and registered office is established at [Panama City / registered agent address], Republic of Panama, where the Foundation's records shall be kept. RESOLVED FURTHER, that Mr/Ms [Name], ID [___], and Mr/Ms [Name], ID [___], are appointed Founder Members of the Foundation Council and, jointly, serve as President and Secretary for a term of [term]. RESOLVED FINALLY, that the Council ratifies the Foundation Charter as registered and authorizes the Secretary to issue certified copies. So agreed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Central Services Department (Ventanilla Única / Online Sede Electrónica)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a formal name reservation application (Solicitud de Certificado de Registro de Nombre) through the Public Registry's physical window or electronic portal. Provide three alternative foundation names, each including the term 'Foundation' or its Spanish equivalent 'Fundación' as permitted, and pay the search fee. Obtain the certificate confirming the name is not confusingly similar to an existing registered foundation, company, or trademark; the certificate is valid for five business days for inscription purposes.
required_dossiers: Name reservation application form
Three proposed alternative names
Copy of the Founder's passport and tax identification data
Proof of payment of the reservation/search fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is denied, elect the next available alternative reserved under the same application; if the full list is rejected, file a new name reservation docket within three business days and reapply with additional alternatives without additional penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public of the First Judicial Circuit of Panama (Official Notary Registry)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Foundation Charter in the Spanish language, specifying the foundation's name, duration, lawful purpose restricted to ISIC 4690 general re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediation, the initial patrimony, the seat of the Foundation Council, the appointment mechanism, and the reservation to the Founder of powers to issue additional regulations if so desired. Have the Founder and the initial Council Members execute the instrument; if executed as a public deed, appear before the Notary and incorporate the instrument into a notarial protocol. The Notary authenticates signatures and issues the first certified copy for registration.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter (private instrument or public deed)
Passport copy and domicile proof of the Founder
Acceptance of office signed by each Foundation Council Member
Evidence of the initial patrimony (bank receipt or escrow certificate)
Notarial fee receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Notary identifies formal defects or the Founder requests post-signature changes, execute a Notarial Amendment (Reforma Adicional) before the same Notary; if the charter is signed abroad, the signatures must be notarized and apostilled under the Hague Convention before presentation to the Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Transfer of Initial Patrimony and Opening of Segregated Trust Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian trust services provider or banking institution holding the segregated account
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a dedicated trust or segregated account in the name of the foundation or, during formation, in the name of the founding law firm for the account of the foundation. Transfer the declared initial patrimony by wire or deposit, obtain a receipt evidencing the credit, and deliver a written escrow discharge letter to the Foundation Council confirming that the initial patrimony is unencumbered and available for the foundation's lawful trade purposes.
required_dossiers: Certified draft of the Foundation Charter
Foundation Council appointment resolution
AML/KYC dossier of the Founder and Council Members
Source-of-funds declaration
Bank or custodian deposit receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank escalates to enhanced due diligence, supply a notarized organizational chart, foundation charter, and source-of-wealth statement; if the deposit is delayed, the foundation's existence is not prejudiced but inscription cannot proceed until the patrimony evidence is available.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Inscription of the Foundation in the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Mercantile Section, Private Interest Foundation Docket (Registro Público de Panamá – Sección Mercantil)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original Foundation Charter together with the notarial certification, serial cover sheet (Hoja de Presentación), certified copies of the supporting patrimony evidence, and the official fee deposit. The Registry examines the legality of the instrument and the lawfulness and non-offensiveness of the foundation's name and purpose. Upon approval, the Registry inscribes the Foundation in the Foundations Volume and issues the foundation number, which constitutes the official legal existence of the Private Interest Foundation.
required_dossiers: Original notarial protocol copy of the Foundation Charter
Name reservation certificate valid for inscription
Evidence of initial patrimony deposit
Registry coversheet and filing form
Official fee payment receipt (USD 250.00)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect note (oficio), file a written clarification and any required charter amendment within three business days; if the defect is incurable, re-notarize a corrected charter and request priority recalculation on the same docket; an adverse denial may be appealed to the Director General of the Public Registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining Certified Registry Copies and Foundation Existence Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama, Certified Copies and Registrar's Office (Firma de Registro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the inscription is perfected, request certified copies of the inscribed Foundation Charter and the Certificate of Existence and Representation (Certificado de Existencia y Representación). Verify that the officer list recorded matches the appointed Foundation Council. If the certified copies will be used outside Panama for bank account opening or transactional purposes, obtain an Apostille from the competent Panamanian authority.
required_dossiers: Inscribed foundation docket number
Certified copy application form
Revenue stamps and certified-copy fee payment
Notarized power of attorney of the requesting representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certified copy is delayed, obtain a provisional plain copy (copia simple) from the registered docket while the certified version is processed; if discrepancies between the charter and registry records appear, present a clarifying Fe de Error resolution through the incorporating counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Operating Notice and Tax Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Revenue Office (Dirección General de Rentas Municipales) of the Municipality of Panama and the General Directorate of Internal Revenue (DGI) of the Ministry of Economy and Finance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Aviso de Operación Municipal for the registered office address, declaring that the Foundation operates solely as a commercial re-invoicing intermediary without a physical industrial plant. When the Foundation generates no Panamanian-source income, notify the DGI of the tax-exempt status applicable to foundations and file the annual flat tax (currently USD 300.00) where required; obtain the RUC only if the Foundation elects to maintain a taxable economic presence in Panama.
required_dossiers: Certified foundation existence certificate
Statement of nature of operations for tariff and trade classification
Lease contract or written consent for the registered office address
Municipal Aviso de Operación application form
DGI tax registration or exemption form
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Municipality questions zoning compatibility, produce the leaseholder's land-use certificate and the fire-safety preapproval; if the DGI challenges the exemption, file the statutory exemption letter under Law No. 25 of 1995 together with proof of payment of the annual foundation flat tax.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: General Directorate of Industries of the Ministry of Commerce and Industries (MICI) and the Municipal Revenue Office of the Municipality of Panama
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Aviso de Operación Municipal (Municipal Commercial Operation Notice), with optional import/export intermediary certification under the Ministry of Commerce and Industries when the Foundation mediates cross-border trade on behalf of clients

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of the Republic of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente – MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt (No EIA required) for pure administrative re-invoicing and offshore trade intermediary operations, as no industrial installation, manufacturing, or hazardous materials processing is conducted; should the Foundation store third-party goods in leased warehouses, a Category I Environmental Certification (Certificado de Categoría I) may be required before warehouse operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater or VOC emissions are generated from the re-invoicing office activity; any domestic sanitary discharges must comply with municipal sewer standards and Executive Decree No. 75 of 2008 water quality criteria; if emergency generators or HVAC cooling equipment are installed, their operation must meet national air quality permissible limits for NOx and CO under MiAMBIENTE regulations and refrigerant-handling obligations under the Montreal Protocol as incorporated in Panamanian law.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Panama Fire Department (Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos) for the registered office spaces; structural load and occupancy certificate for the leased premises verified by the Municipal Curaduría; and workplace hygiene and occupational health clearance from the Ministry of Labor and Labor Development (MITRADEL) for any locally engaged employees.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance, at the taxpayer portal 'Sede Electrónica del Contribuyente' (https://dgi.mef.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Private Interest Foundation (PIF) must be validly incorporated and registered in the Panamanian Public Registry and maintain a resident agent. For tax registration, the PIF files an application with the DGI using Form 600 (Registro Único de Contribuyente), attaching the foundation charter, Public Registry filing certificate, resident agent acceptance, registered commercial domicile, and resolution by the Foundation Council identifying the founder and beneficiaries. The DGI issues a RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) for income tax and ITBMS purposes, and the foundation must register for e-invoicing/fiscal receipt obligations before commencing commercial activity.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama does not provide US-style check-the-box elections or hybrid mismatch elections under domestic law. The PIF is a distinct legal entity taxed on its Panamanian-source income. A PIF may elect to be administered under simplified reporting rules for foreign-source assets and is not required or permitted to elect pass-through treatment for income tax; any founder/beneficiary attribution rules apply only to Panamanian-source distributions under the Tax Code. Group consolidation and accelerated depreciation elections exist for domestic corporate groups, but no elective transparency classification is available for PIFs.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto a la Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general exemption threshold for ITBMS registration; any person engaging in taxable transfers of goods or taxable services in Panama, or importing goods/rendering services subject to the tax, must register. A simplified small-taxpayer regime applies to natural persons whose annual gross turnover does not exceed B/.36,000, allowing reduced compliance obligations rather than exemption from ITBMS.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama has adopted a mandatory electronic invoicing and fiscal clearance regime administered by the DGI under the 'Factura Electrónica de Panamá' (FEP) framework, developed through Executive Decree No. 119 of 13 July 2020 and subsequent DGI resolutions. Affected taxpayers must issue invoices in XML through an authorized e-invoicing system integrated with the DGI platform, transmit invoice data in near real time via the SIFE (Sistema de Facturación Electrónica), and obtain a digital authorization/stamp from the DGI before issuance. The mandate is phased by taxpayer category, and exporters or large taxpayers must comply with API/web-service integration, digital signature, and DGI clearance requirements for every invoice.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: ITBMS is zero-rated for goods physically exported from Panamanian customs territory, provided the export is directed to a foreign destination and is supported by a valid customs export declaration. Services are zero-rated when rendered in Panama but effectively utilized outside Panama, performed for a non-resident recipient who derives no economic benefit from Panamanian consumption, or expressly classified as an exported service under DGI criteria. For a general re-invoicing intermediary, income from goods that never enter Panamanian territory falls outside the territorial scope of income tax; ITBMS also does not attach to foreign-to-foreign transactions when the service is economically consumed abroad.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Airway Bill
Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export proceeds
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating is subject to documentary audit by DGI and the National Customs Authority. False documentation, simulated exports, or indirect reuse of zero-rated goods in the domestic market triggers retroactive ITBMS liability, plus monthly interest, surcharges of up to 50% of the tax evaded, and administrative fines of up to B/.50,000. Directors and resident agents may be jointly liable where the exporter acts with intent to evade. Criminal sanctions under the Panamanian Tax Criminal Law (Law 50 of 2017) include imprisonment for fiscal fraud; the clawback period is generally extended to six years from the date the false declaration was filed.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: No central bank; Panama operates a dollarized currency system under the US dollar as legal tender. Banking supervision is vested in the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP). The Ministry of Economy and Finance oversees fiscal policy but does not administer exchange controls.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama has full convertibility on both current and capital account, with no exchange control law and no distinction between resident and non-resident accounts. Profit remittance, dividend distributions, and capital repatriation are freely permitted, subject only to applicable Panamanian taxes (e.g., territorial income tax) and anti-money laundering reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender requirements exist. Exporters and trading intermediaries may freely retain, use, or remit export proceeds in US dollars without mandatory conversion or repatriation timelines, though commercial banks apply standard reportable transaction thresholds to the Financial Analysis Unit (UAF) for AML/CFT purposes.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium. Panama is not a licensed Electronic Money Institution (EMI) regime, and offshore EMI accounts (e.g., UK/EU e-money platforms) generally restrict onboarding of Private Interest Foundations due to the lack of public beneficial ownership and the inherent use of re-invoicing trading structures. Such accounts are viable only as ancillary payment wallets for low-volume receivables, not as primary treasury rails, and may require a maintained link to a domestic bank account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Banks operating under SBP regulations typically require physical presence of the foundation's beneficial owner(s) or a duly authorized legal representative for the initial KYC interview. Remote onboarding is possible only on a case-by-case basis for lower-risk profiles; in practice, most Tier-1 Panamanian banks will require a physical meeting in Panama or with a consular delegation. A local registered agent and a physical office (virtual office per bank policy) are mandatory for account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foundation structure with no statutory annual filing and no standard corporate registry outside the private foundation registry.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Authenticated and apostilled foundation charter; registered agent certificate; notarized statement of pour-pour nomine (beneficial ownership); legal tax status certificate; business plan with expected volume and counterparty list; source-of-wealth documentation for the founder.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBOs and multi-jurisdiction re-invoicing flows with no physical operational footprint.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Lease or services agreement with a Panamanian administrative office; UBO's passport copy and proof-of-address (utilities, bank statement); bank reference letters; detailed fluxogram of trade transactions; copy of underlying ISIC 4690 supply/purchase contracts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid high-turnover in trade receipts without clear commercial rationale or with third-party payments.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Fully executed commercial contracts (PO and invoice); bill-of-lading / airway bill; transport insurance certificate; customs declarations (DUA); banks' internal trade-finance questionnaire and transaction-level spreadsheet.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure to sanctioned or high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., Venezuela, Russia, Cuba).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Letter of explanation of legitimate goods flow; complete transaction chain evidence (from ultimate buyer to ultimate supplier); sanctions screening results; bank-approved country restriction matrix; commitment to use only USD-denominated accounts.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital for the PIF must be wired via SWIFT MT103 to the foundation's Panamanian operative account. Purpose code '8903' (Capital Contribution) is recommended for shareholder/founder endowment; for trading advances, use 'Investment Tied to Trade' or 'Trade Pre-Payment' with the underlying contract reference. All inbound wires are subject to UAF reporting over USD 10,000 and require a source-of-funds statement and, for loans, a flexibly evidenced intercompany loan agreement to avoid recharacterization as equity.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound supplier payments settle via SWIFT MT103 for telegraphic transfers, or via Commercial Letter of Credit (UCP600) for goods under documentary trade. MT202 COV must be used when passing onward from the Panamanian bank to a third correspondent. Payment messages must include full invoice number, trade contract reference, and clear description of goods (HS code) to prevent FATF red flags and comply with SBP's Regulation No. 003-2022 on trade finance transparency.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable Forwards (USD vs Latin American currencies) via Panamanian or US correspondent banks
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) on currencies without free convertibility (e.g., CNY, ARS, VES) through ISDA/CSA-approved banks
Cross-currency swaps (CCS) with foreign exchange hedging mandate, entered under Paris or New York law ISDA master agreement

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Franchise Tax / Annuity (Tasa Anual de Funcionamiento)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministry of Economy and Finance
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 15 July each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment: automatic 10% surcharge plus monthly interest of 1%; entity loses good-standing certificate (paz y salvo) and access to registry services; continued non-payment for 3 consecutive years permits the Public Registry to mark the foundation inactive, and the DGI may initiate judicial collection proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Anual de Renta) - Territorial/Nil Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 15 April following the calendar year, or per the DGI grouped RUC filing schedule; final-month extension procedures apply
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing: fine of 10% of any tax due (minimum USD 50, maximum per Tax Code) plus monthly interest of 1%; a nil return filed late triggers a fixed administrative penalty of USD 100; persistent non-compliance may lead to a tax-visit order and blocking of certificates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO / Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Declaración de Beneficiario Final vinculada a la anualidad)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGI - Beneficial Ownership Registry (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Same deadline as the Annual Franchise Tax (on or before 15 July); updates within 15 calendar days of any ownership, council, or protector change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update the UBO declaration: administrative fines up to USD 5,000 under Law 129 of 2020 and Executive Decree 607 of 2021; suspension of the foundation's access to Public Registry transaction services until compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory audit is required only when the foundation's Panamanian-source gross annual income exceeds USD 1,000,000 or total gross assets exceed USD 3,000,000, or when the foundation engages in regulated local activities (banking, insurance, trust services). Otherwise no annual audit is legally mandatory.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Panama Tax Code and Law 25 of 1995 require foundational accounts to reflect assets, liabilities, rights, and operations; financial statements must follow Panama GAAP (IFRS as adopted by the Colegio de Contadores Públicos de Panamá) or IFRS for SMEs for smaller entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, the foundation's legal representative or registered agent renews the beneficial ownership data by accessing the DGI's annual compliance screen associated with the franchise tax payment to confirm the founder, all members of the Foundation Council, the protector, and every natural-person beneficiary holding a direct or indirect interest of 10% or more. Changes occurring during the year must be communicated to the registered agent and electronically filed with the DGI within 15 calendar days.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries / Book of Holdings (beneficiary names and contributions)
Register of Foundation Council Members and Protectors
Minute Book (Foundation Council resolutions and protector directives)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 300 - USD 750 (standard Panama registered agent and registered office services for a re-invoicing PIF)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - USD 5,000 (when a voluntary audit is engaged for banking facilities or if a threshold is triggered)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial system: only Panamanian-source income is taxed; foreign-source re-invoicing margin is effectively exempt. A Private Interest Foundation (PIF) is outside the corporate income tax net for assets and activities performed outside Panama, paying only an annual franchise fee of USD 400. Special regimes (Colon Free Zone, Panama Pacifico, Multinational Headquarters) can reduce CIT to 0-5% on approved in-jurisdiction activities.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 102 (Declaración de Renta de Personas Jurídicas) filed through the Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) online portal under MEF's 'T@-Banco' system
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within the first 3 months after fiscal year-end; for calendar-year entities, no later than 31 March of the following year

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross revenues arising from sources located in Panama, including commissions, margins from re-invoicing, and sales of goods delivered in Panama.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PIF engaged in pure offshore re-invoicing should report zero here unless goods or services physically enter or are used in Panama; invoices routed overseas are not Panamanian-source income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 / Line 2 - Cost of Sales and Deductible Expenses
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim costs and expenses directly attributable to generation of Panamanian-source income, supported by electronic invoicing and bank wire documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For re-invoicing operations, intercompany purchases may be deducted only where title passes in Panama; cost allocations to the PIF require contemporaneous transfer pricing analysis.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computed as Box 1 less Box 2; if negative, declare zero and support with loss carryforward schedule.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A properly structured offshore PIF with no Panamanian activity will show zero; do not offset foreign losses against Panamanian-source gains.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Multiply Box 3 by 25%; apply any authorized preferential rate for licensed zones.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If Box 3 is zero, enter zero. If any Panamanian-source royalty or service fee exists, apply the general rate, unless a special regime applies.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 5 / Line 5 - Advance Payments, Credits, Withholdings
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: List prepaid income tax instalments, Panamanian source tax withheld by clients, and authorized tax credits (e.g., reforestation, donation).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders have no withholding credit here unless Panama has collected dividend or royalty withholding inside the company; attach DGI-issued certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Line 6 - Net Tax Payable / Refund Claim
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Box 4 minus Box 5; if positive, payment must be settled via the DGI e-payment system at filing.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A zero or negative result requires no payment; a negative result may be carried as a credit only if supported by a formal DGI refund request.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing is penalized at 10% of the tax due (minimum USD 50). A monthly surcharge of 1% applies on unpaid tax (capped at 12%). Interest runs at 10% per annum. Filing with false facts attracts a 100% enhancement and criminal tax evasion charges if fraudulent intent is shown.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced DTA rate, the shareholder must submit to the paying Panamanian entity the Tax Residency Certificate (CRF) issued by the shareholder's tax authority and a Form 310 declaration of beneficial ownership before the distribution date. The payer then applies the applicable treaty rate at source; refunds are made through the DGI's International Tax Office within 15 months if the documents are irregular or submitted late.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Panamanian-source royalties: 10% statutory, reduced to 5-10% under relevant DTA (Article 12). Panamanian-source interest: 5% statutory, reduced to 0% under several DTAs and for interest paid to qualified foreign financial institutions; interest generated wholly outside Panama is not subject to withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory when cross-border related-party transactions exceed US$3 million in the fiscal year; Master File is required when the worldwide group revenue exceeds US$50 million. A transfer pricing disclosure (Form 820-TF) must be filed if aggregate related-party transactions exceed US$250,000.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama endorses the OECD Inclusive Framework and Law 120 of 2018 codifies substance-over-form and transfer pricing rules with automatic CFC-style adjustments for no-substance shell entities. Although Panama has no BVI-style ESR, the Tax Administration may disregard a PIF's separate juridical personality if it lacks physical premises, payroll, bank accounts, and board minutes evidencing core re-invoicing functions in Panama. A re-invoicing hub with no operational substance is recharacterized as a sham and assessed on gross revenue rather than net margin.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to declare Panamanian-source re-invoicing income or artificially moving a taxable Panamanian transaction to foreign books to avoid Form 102 filing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 50% to 200% of the understated tax (Article 605-A Tax Code); criminal conviction under Article 169 of the Penal Code carries 3 to 7 years imprisonment and a fine of USD 10,000 to USD 100,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false returns are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax deficiency; the DGI may request preventive travel bans, freeze personal accounts, and confiscate personal property under the statutory clawback procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Setting re-invoicing markups or service fees outside the arm's length range, or failing to prepare and file the annual transfer pricing return despite crossing threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Primary adjustment adds back up to 25% tax on the adjusted profit; secondary penalties of 10% to 20% of the transaction amount are imposed under Law 120/2018, plus interest at 10% per annum. Habitual non-compliance triggers loss of all tax incentives and a mandatory audit for 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Board members who approved transfer pricing policies without financial analysis can be assessed personally for the secondary penalty; serious disgorgement orders may be entered, and directors can be disqualified from serving on any Panamanian company for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Pure Re-Invoicing PIF with no physical office, no employees in Panama, no board meetings, no operational records, and using only a domiciliation service; the entity acts as a conduit while the actual purchase orders are executed by offshore principals.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the PIF as a transparent entity; the full invoice value is treated as taxable income, subject to 25% corporate income tax plus 10% dividend withholding on the deemed distribution; registration may be cancelled after three consecutive defaults of the annual substance declaration. Fines of up to USD 100,000 under Law 120/2018 for failure to maintain economic substance records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are personally liable for taxes recharacterized on the shell entity and may face civil restitution claims from creditors or foreign revenue authorities; the Panamanian registry may impose a travel ban and place the director's name on the 'Compliance Risk List' for 5 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the re-invoicing structure to process fraudulent invoices, cyclically transfer funds through Swift LC/TT/XT rails with no real goods crossing, sustaining artificial payment turnovers, or accepting third-party payments into the PIF account without executing the contract.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines under Decree 196/2019 and Law 41/2000 range from USD 10,000 to USD 1,000,000 per violation; criminal liability under Law 201/2017 for trade-based money laundering applies, with imprisonment of 5 to 12 years and confiscation of the instrumentalities and proceeds up to triple the laundered value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who fail to implement robust KYC, invoice inspection, and source-of-funds verification are criminally liable under the corporate criminal veil-Piercing doctrine; they may receive travel bans, asset freezes, and 5 to 10 year prison sentences. Civil damages are recoverable from their estates in favor of victims or the Panamanian Financial Unit.
